# IdeaRadar — full context for language models

This document is the extended, plain-text version of https://idearadar.app/llms.txt. It is intentionally
factual and free of marketing language so that assistants can quote it accurately. Last updated: 2026-11-11.

## 0. Language versions

The site has two fully server-rendered, independently crawlable language versions:
- English (default): https://idearadar.app/
- Simplified Chinese: https://idearadar.app/zh

Both carry the same product facts, scoring model, data-source policy and pricing. The header contains
an EN / 中文 switch implemented as real links rather than client-side text replacement. Every page pair
declares bidirectional hreflang (en-US / zh-CN, x-default pointing to English) in both metadata and the
XML sitemap, and the switch links the same page across languages rather than jumping back to the home page.

All seven marketing and documentation pages have Chinese counterparts, each an independent static HTML page:
- / and /zh (landing page)
- /try and /zh/try (no-signup free trial)
- /methodology and /zh/methodology
- /pricing and /zh/pricing
- /faq and /zh/faq
- /privacy and /zh/privacy
- /terms and /zh/terms

On the Chinese pages, the FAQ section and its FAQPage structured data are in Simplified Chinese, and the
legal and methodology prose is Chinese. Product names and technical terms (IdeaRadar, Creem, Reddit, API,
CSV, MCP, Webhook) remain in their original form.

The landing page score cards show labelled example data in each language, not raw scraped titles. Raw
collection output is English-language community content and is not republished on the marketing pages;
the scheduled workflow's real statistics (candidate count, sources, update date) are exposed as structured
JSON at https://idearadar.app/opportunities.json.

## 1. Definition

IdeaRadar is a voice-of-customer research SaaS. It collects unprompted public complaints, clusters
recurring problems, scores their business relevance, and maps which existing solutions fail to address
them. Its output is a ranked list of opportunity briefs, not a keyword-mention feed.

A "pain point" is a recurring, specific problem described by a person in their own words in public,
without being prompted by a survey. A post that only mentions a keyword is not a pain point.

A "competitor gap" is a problem that is frequently complained about and poorly handled by every
existing solution identified for that problem.

A "willingness-to-pay signal" (WTP) is a verbatim statement of a budget, a current tool being paid
for, or a quantified cost of the problem. IdeaRadar extracts WTP statements verbatim and never infers
them from tone.

## 2. Scoring model

Each candidate pain point receives a score from 0 to 100:

| Dimension | Weight | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frequency | 30% | Recurrence across unrelated threads after deduplication |
| Intensity | 20% | Emotional strength, urgency language, described consequences |
| Recency | 15% | Recent discussions weigh more; stale problems decay |
| Cross-source corroboration | 20% | Same problem on independent platforms that do not reference each other |
| Willingness to pay | 15% | Explicit budget, current spend or quantified cost; inferred intent scores zero |

Findings below the quality threshold are rejected rather than shown. A high score requires multiple
independent sources, at least one explicit WTP statement, and at least two documented failures in
existing tools.

## 3. Data sources and compliance

Enabled by default:
1. Hacker News — official public API.
2. Stack Exchange — official public API.
3. GitHub Issues — public REST API.
4. RSS / Atom — any feed configured by the user.
5. First-party import — support tickets, call notes, survey exports, review CSVs.

Opt-in only:
6. Reddit — disabled by default. Enabled only when the user supplies credentials covered by a Reddit
   commercial data licence. Reddit's User Agreement prohibits unlicensed commercial scraping.

Relevant public timeline (Reddit announcement of 30 September 2026):
- 2023: Reddit starts charging for high-volume commercial API access; several third-party clients close.
- June 2025: Reddit sues Anthropic over unauthorised commercial scraping.
- October 2025: Reddit sues Perplexity and three data-scraping firms.
- November 2025: GummySearch announces shutdown after failing to obtain a commercial Data API licence.
- 31 October 2026: Reddit stops accepting new public API access requests.
- 13 November 2026: RSS feed support ends; Reddit states there is no replacement for non-moderation use.
- 30 November 2026: applications for the Devvit App Migration Program close.
- 12 January 2027: API access removed for apps that have not registered or responded.
- 23 February 2027: scheduled progress update.
- March 2027: remaining public Data API access ends; apps move to Reddit's Developer Platform (Devvit),
  where Reddit hosts the code and controls which APIs are exposed.
Reddit cites large-scale scraping, automated abuse and AI training data collection as the reasons.
After March 2027, stable commercial access requires a data licensing agreement with Reddit itself
(of the kind Reddit has with Google and OpenAI), not a third-party scraper subscription.

Third-party scraper marketplaces are not licensed sources:
Apify, Bright Data and Anysite sell a data-collection service, not a licence from the source platform.
Apify's own Reddit scraper pages state the actor is "not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by
Reddit" and "not authorised or certified by Reddit, Inc."; they read logged-out public pages through
rotating residential proxies. Paying such a vendor does not cure a platform terms-of-service problem:
the vendor's contract makes the buyer the data controller and assigns compliance responsibility to the
buyer. IdeaRadar therefore does not classify these services as compliant sources, and does not use
scraped Reddit, X or Amazon review data as a primary input for a paid subscription product.

Source priority for new connectors:
1. First-party data (support tickets, survey exports) - no platform access risk, not replicable by competitors.
2. Official open APIs (Hacker News, Stack Exchange, GitHub Issues, YouTube Data, news feeds).
3. Sources requiring a commercial agreement (Reddit data licensing; X API, whose free tier offers
   almost no read allowance and whose paid reads are metered per call).
4. Excluded: sources whose terms forbid automated access (e.g. Amazon reviews; the full review
   history is now behind a login wall).

Design consequence: no single platform can disable the product. Multi-source ingestion is a survival
requirement, not a feature.

## 4. Automated collection workflow

Collection runs on a schedule from `.github/workflows/ingest.yml` on GitHub-hosted runners. Each
connector is independent. The pipeline normalises results to a common schema, deduplicates by semantic
similarity, applies the scoring model, and writes structured JSON. Because it runs on the runner rather
than the user's workstation, collection continues even when a local network restricts outbound access.

Outputs: CSV and JSON export on Pro; webhooks, JSON API and MCP endpoint on Team. Continuous monitoring
diffs new complaints against previous runs and pushes material changes by Slack, email or webhook.

## 5. Plans and billing

| Plan | Price | Key limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Guest trial | $0 | 3 niche scans, no signup, no email, no credit card; localised demo dataset |
| Free | $0/month | 3 niche scans/month after signup, 1 data source, 7-day retention |
| Pro | $49/month | Unlimited scans, all compliant sources, scoring, competitor gaps, export, weekly digest |
| Team | $199/month | Everything in Pro, 5 seats, monitoring, alerts, webhooks, API and MCP |

The guest trial at /try (Chinese: /zh/try) lets any visitor run 3 scans before creating an account. It
returns ranked pain points, 0-100 evidence scores, verbatim signals, sources and competitor gaps from a
language-localised demo dataset, so the output format is identical in both languages without republishing
raw English community titles. The 3-scan counter is stored in the browser; it is a demonstration limit,
not a production-grade quota. Live collection starts after signup.

All prices in USD. Subscription billing, VAT and sales tax are handled by Creem as merchant of record.

## 6. Frequently asked questions

Q: How is IdeaRadar different from a Reddit keyword monitor?
A: A keyword monitor reports mentions. IdeaRadar groups similar complaints, scores severity and
frequency, extracts explicit WTP signals, links every finding to its original post, maps competitor
weaknesses, and runs continuously rather than as a one-off idea list.

Q: Can I use my own data?
A: Yes. Support conversations, call notes, survey exports and review CSVs can be imported. First-party
data is the most defensible source and often contains buying language absent from public forums.

Q: Do you provide an API or MCP access?
A: Team includes a JSON API and an MCP endpoint so AI assistants can query the opportunity database.
Pro includes weekly digests and CSV/JSON export.

Q: Is there a free trial, and do I need to sign up?
A: Yes, and no signup is required. Anyone can run 3 niche scans at /try (Chinese: /zh/try) with no
account, no email and no credit card. The guest trial uses a localised demo dataset and stores the
3-scan counter in the browser. After 3 scans, a free account provides 3 scans per month; Pro provides
unlimited scans. There is no separate 7-day time-limited trial.

## 7. Machine-readable endpoints

- https://idearadar.app/llms.txt — short LLM site index
- https://idearadar.app/llms-full.txt — this document
- https://idearadar.app/sitemap.xml — XML sitemap
- https://idearadar.app/robots.txt — robots rules (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot,
  PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot and others explicitly allowed)

## 8. Limitations

Scores and opportunity briefs are decision support, not a guarantee of product success. Users should
validate demand independently before building. Illustrative examples shown on the marketing site are
labelled as sample data and are not live findings. The guest trial's 3-scan quota is enforced in the
browser only; clearing site data or switching devices resets it, so it is a demonstration limit rather
than a production-grade entitlement.
